questions.stem: An AuditLog singleton keeps `private static AuditLog instance;`, which a synchronized getInstance() fills on first call, and its private constructor throws if `instance != null`. At start-up a framework scans the package and calls each class's no-arg constructor through reflection, before any code has called getInstance(). Later the service calls getInstance(). How many AuditLog objects now exist?

options.text: Two, since the check read a field that was still null when the framework's call ran
options.says: the lazy field is set only by getInstance(), so a reflective call that comes first passes the guard, and getInstance() then builds another

options.text: Two, since code in a private constructor is skipped when reflection calls it
options.says: setAccessible(true) only switches off the access check; the constructor body, guard included, runs

options.text: One, since the check throws on the framework's call and getInstance() builds the only one
options.says: the guard throws only when the field is set, and nothing had set it when the framework called

options.text: One, since getInstance() returns the object that the framework's call built
options.says: the reflective call doesn't store its object in the field, so getInstance() finds null and builds a new one

origin.section: A Private Constructor Stops new, and Nothing Else

questions.stem: A FeatureFlags singleton implements Serializable. Its `static final FeatureFlags INSTANCE` is built eagerly, its private constructor throws if INSTANCE is already set, and it declares no serialization methods. A cluster node receives a replicated session that holds the flags object and reads it. What does the session on that node hold?

options.text: The node's existing INSTANCE, since static fields aren't written, so reading takes the local one
options.says: static fields are not written, but reading still builds a new object from the instance fields unless readResolve returns INSTANCE

options.text: The node's existing INSTANCE, since the constructor's check makes reading fall back to the instance already built
options.says: reading never calls the class's constructor, so the guard has no say

options.text: A second FeatureFlags object, since reading builds the object without calling the class's constructor
options.says: deserialization allocates the object and fills its fields, running only the no-arg constructor of the first non-serializable superclass

options.text: A second FeatureFlags object, since reading calls the constructor before INSTANCE is initialized on that node
options.says: the constructor isn't called at all while reading; the class's initialization ran its constructor once

origin.section: Deserialization Makes a Second Instance Without Running the Constructor

questions.stem: Two web applications are deployed to one servlet container. Each bundles pricing-core.jar in its WEB-INF/lib, and the container doesn't have the jar on its own class path. The jar declares `enum RateCache { INSTANCE; ... }`, and each application puts prices into RateCache.INSTANCE. What does each application read back?

options.text: Both applications' prices, since an enum's constants are created once per JVM
options.says: an enum constant is a static field of its class, and each application's loader defines its own RateCache class

options.text: Both applications' prices, since each application's loader asks the container's loader, which defines RateCache once
options.says: the container's loader can't find a class that isn't on its class path, so each application's loader defines its own

options.text: Only the prices it put in, since each application's loader defines a separate RateCache class
options.says: a class is identified by its name and its defining loader, so two loaders give two classes and two constants

options.text: Only the prices it put in, since the container runs each application in a separate JVM
options.says: a servlet container runs its applications in one JVM; the separation comes from their class loaders

origin.section: Each Class Loader Has Its Own Singleton, Enum Included

questions.stem: ConfigSnapshot keeps its one instance in a private nested class, `private static final class Holder { static final ConfigSnapshot INSTANCE = new ConfigSnapshot(); }`, returned by getInstance(). It implements Serializable and has no other additions. A cache writes getInstance() out and reads it back. What comes back?

options.text: The existing instance, since Holder.INSTANCE is static final and can't be assigned a second object
options.says: reading never assigns Holder.INSTANCE; it builds a separate object that nothing stores in that field

options.text: The existing instance, since the class-initialization lock that guards Holder also guards reading
options.says: that lock makes the holder lazy and thread-safe; it has no part in deserialization

options.text: A second ConfigSnapshot, since reading initializes the Holder class again and builds a new INSTANCE
options.says: a class is initialized once per loader; the second object is built by deserialization, not by Holder

options.text: A second ConfigSnapshot, since reading allocates a new object and fills its fields without consulting Holder
options.says: the holder idiom gives laziness and safe initialization only; deserialization builds its own object, and without readResolve that object is returned

origin.section: The Holder Idiom Chooses When the Instance Is Built; Only the Enum Refuses Copies

questions.stem: A TokenStore singleton is reached through TokenStore.getInstance(). Its tests failed depending on their order, so every test class now calls TokenStore.resetForTesting() in @BeforeEach. Later the team turns on JUnit's parallel execution. What happens to the TokenStore tests?

options.text: They stay green, since each test running at the same time starts from a freshly reset store
options.says: a reset at the start doesn't help a test whose neighbour, running at the same time, changes the shared store

options.text: They stay green, since tests running at the same time each see the static field of their own thread
options.says: a static field is one per class per class loader, shared by every thread

options.text: They fail now and then, since a test running at the same time can change the store another is using
options.says: the reset only works while tests run one at a time; parallel tests use and reset the same instance

options.text: They fail now and then, since a test running at the same time loads TokenStore again and misses the reset
options.says: classes are defined per class loader, not per thread; every test in the JVM shares the one store

origin.section: A Static Singleton Carries One Test's State Into the Next
